test:
RULE written_at=2026-10-11T23:07:58Z (read from the clock, before any fund is classed; only record totals and not_established were read)

UNIT. A read unit is record A's: the by/sl rows of one account, one effective day, one fund, one kind (purchase/sale), summed, with a served close on that day (guard |Quantity|>=0.05 per row). ratio = |Quantity| x served close / |Amount| (served close over price paid), dev = |ratio-1|. gap = |Amount| - |Quantity| x close (dollars; positive on a purchase = paid above the close; negative on a sale = received below the close).

UNIT STATUS (every read unit has exactly one):
 PASS: dev <= 0.01.
 UNRESOLVED (counts as neither pass nor fail): (a) 0.01 < dev <= 0.05 for either kind and either direction, because a neighbouring day's close or a flat charge puts a unit there with a right close (record B: 46 of 246 off purchase rows have a prior/next-day close within 1 percent; record B section 6 post hoc flat dollar charge); (b) a PURCHASE with ratio < 1 and dev <= 0.0575 (the largest front load, record A not_established: up to 5.75 percent); (c) CHARGE-SIZED: dev > 0.01, the gap in the charge direction (purchase: Amount > shares x close; sale: Amount < shares x close) and gap <= 34.15 dollars (the largest constant, 34, of record B section 6 plus its 0.15 tolerance; that list was read off the rows, post hoc, a description not a test; it is used here ONLY to take units OUT of the failing count, never to pass a fund).
 FAIL: every other unit with dev > 0.01, i.e. dev > 0.05 not charge-sized (a sale is NEVER excused by a front load: rule (b) is purchase only), and a purchase with ratio >= 1 or a sale of any direction with dev > 0.05 and not charge-sized. Over-20 percent units fail outright in either direction unless charge-sized. 5-to-20 percent units fail unless a purchase within 5.75 percent below the close, or charge-sized. 1-to-5 percent units never fail.
 DECISIVE units = PASS + FAIL units.

failing_band: "dev>5% fails (purchase below the close: dev>5.75%) unless charge-sized (gap<=34.15 USD in the charge direction); 1-5% never fails and never passes; a sale is not excused by a front load"

CLASS (per fund series, in this order):
 1. no_trade_row: zero read units. (Two reason codes kept inside the class, in the JSON: no purchase/sale row at all; purchase/sale rows all before the series' first stored close. The five classes sum to 270.)
 2. too_few: at least one read unit but fewer than minimum_rows=5 decisive units, or decisive units on fewer than 3 distinct effective days.
 3. fails: fail share = FAIL / DECISIVE > share_fails = 0.50.
 4. passes: fail share <= 0.10 AND the guard below is met.
 5. mixed: fail share > 0.10 and <= 0.50; and a fund with share <= 0.10 whose guard is not met is too_few (see guard).

minimum_rows = 5 (decisive units) and at least 3 distinct effective days. Why: one trade can be a bad print or a flat charge on a small amount, and all accounts that trade on one day see the same close, so units on one day are one piece of evidence; with 5 decisive units one unit is 20 percent of the evidence, below the 50 percent fail line, so a single odd unit can move a fund to mixed but never to fails; 3 days so a single day's close cannot class a fund by itself.

share_fails = 0.50. Why: fails means the served close misses the price paid on a majority of the fund's decisive trades; a series wrong on most of its trades is not the unadjusted close, a series wrong on a minority is a partial defect and is mixed. The pass line 0.10 is twenty times the rate at which the substituted control misses (record A totals: 6 over-20 plus 45 in 5-to-20 of 10636 units, 0.5 percent), leaving room for a small fund's bad prints. Neither line was chosen by how many funds it moves; both were fixed before any per-fund count was read.

GUARD (d), recent window: an adjusted series converges to the traded price near the present, so units near the present cannot show that a series is unadjusted. Window = effective day within 180 calendar days of the latest served-close date in the 270-series table (180 days: a half-year of distributions is about 1-2 percent for a 2-4 percent yielding fund, the size of the 1 percent band). A fund can be classed passes only if it has at least 5 decisive units on at least 3 distinct effective days that are BEFORE the window start; otherwise a fund with fail share <= 0.10 is too_few. The guard never restricts fails or mixed (a failure in the window is stronger evidence, not weaker).

VBTLX: classed by this rule like every fund and carried in the csv like every fund; excluded from every count by the CTO until its cause has a name: the five counts include it where the rule puts it (so they sum to 270); if it is a fail it is in named with excluded=true (len(named)==fails); flagged in the JSON key excluded and in the md.

SENSITIVITY (marked not the result, reported only after the classing): (1) charge-sized excuse off; (2) pass line 0.05 and 0.20; (3) fail line 0.40 and 0.60; (4) minimum_rows 3 and 10; (5) guard window 365 days and off.

Presence counts a held trading day present when dell1's object carries a non-null as_traded_close on that date. Dell1's values were not compared with any vendor source; this is a read of the object, not a check of its prices.
The three partial objects (GFFFX, FOCPX, FCNTX; lock valid_from 2026-04-14) hold no row before 2026-04-14. Why the lock starts there is not read; whether dell1 will extend it is dell1's to say.
